screens.title: Fractions you already speak
lines: A decimal is a fraction with a secret denominator: 0.7 = 7/10, 0.37 = 37/100, 0.123 = 123/1000.
Each place right of the point is 10× smaller — tenths, hundredths, thousandths. The point is just the landmark.

vocab.meaning: what a digit is worth because of WHERE it sits

screens.framing: No grade, no pressure — just try it. Your money sense and your fraction sense both want to help.

screens.title: The point that hops
lines: Multiply by 10, 100, 1000 and every digit slides left — the point seems to hop right: 3.7 × 100 = 370.
To divide BY a decimal, slide BOTH points until the divisor is whole: 6 ÷ 0.2 becomes 60 ÷ 2. Same answer, friendlier numbers.

items.prompt: Explorer's Gambit: what is 0.3 + 0.07? Trust your place-value instincts.
items.hint: 0.3 is 3 tenths — which is 30 hundredths. Now both numbers speak hundredths.
items.explanation: 0.30 + 0.07 = 0.37 — line up the decimal points and every place finds its partner.

items.prompt: Let's map the decimal kingdom: places, padding, and the lining-up rule.

steps.text: Right of the decimal point, each place is 10× smaller: tenths, hundredths, thousandths. In 4.275 that's 2 tenths, 7 hundredths, 5 thousandths.
Padding trick: 0.3 = 0.30 = 0.300. Trailing zeros AFTER the point change nothing — that's how 0.3 and 0.07 can finally line up.
Add with the points aligned: 0.30 + 0.07 = 0.37. Subtract the same way: 1.50 − 0.32 = 1.18.
And every decimal is a fraction in disguise: 0.37 = 37/100. Your fraction powers transfer completely.

items.prompt: Your turn at the bake-sale till: a brownie costs $2.45 and a lemon bar costs $0.80. Total?

lines: Line up the decimal points, then add: 2.45 + 0.80

items.hint: 45 hundredths + 80 hundredths regroups into a fresh dollar.
items.explanation: 2.45 + 0.80 = 3.25 — the aligned points kept dollars with dollars and cents with cents.

items.prompt: A new skein holds 5.2 m of yarn, and Amal's mitten pattern uses 3.75 m. How much yarn is left?

lines: Pad to hundredths so the columns match: 5.2 → [[5.20|5.2]]

items.hint: Give 5.2 a trailing zero first — then subtract column by column.
items.explanation: 5.20 − 3.75 = 1.45 m — padding with a zero made the regrouping honest.

items.prompt: Dividing BY a decimal: how many 0.25 m tassel cords can Amal cut from 3 m of yarn?

steps.text: The question 'how many 0.25s fit in 3?' is the division 3 ÷ 0.25.
Make the divisor whole: slide BOTH decimal points two places right. 3 ÷ 0.25 becomes 300 ÷ 25.

check.question: Why is sliding both points fair?
options: Both numbers were multiplied by 100, so the quotient stays the same
Only the divisor changed, and that's allowed

check.question: Why is the answer BIGGER than 3?
options: We multiplied by 100 and forgot to undo it
Each cord is shorter than 1 m, so more pieces fit

steps.text: Sanity check: 12 × 0.25 = 3 ✓. Dividing by a number smaller than 1 gives you MORE pieces — let that feel normal.

items.prompt: Multiplying decimals: a K-pop photocard sticker sheet measures 0.4 m by 0.6 m. Find its area.

lines: Count decimal places: 0.4 has 1 and 0.6 has 1, so the product needs [[2]]

items.hint: Multiply the digits first; place the point last.
items.explanation: Tenths × tenths make hundredths: 0.4 × 0.6 = 0.24 — counting places put the point exactly where it belongs.

items.prompt: Potions class: a 7 L cauldron is poured into 0.5 L bottles. Finish the solve.
items.hint: Make the divisor whole first — both numbers ride the same slide.
items.explanation: 70 ÷ 5 = 14 bottles, and 14 × 0.5 = 7 ✓ — half-liter bottles mean twice as many as liters.

items.prompt: Last one — you drive. Three friends split a $7.74 cookie-ingredient bill equally. How much does each pay?
items.hint: Divide place by place: 7 ones, then 7 tenths, then 14 hundredths.
items.explanation: 7.74 ÷ 3 = 2.58, and the multiply-back check proves every cent landed safely.

items.prompt: In the number 3.247, which digit sits in the thousandths place?
items.hint: March right of the point: tenths, hundredths, thousandths.
items.explanation: After the point comes 2 (tenths), 4 (hundredths), 7 (thousandths) — position is everything.

items.prompt: Write 'six tenths' as a decimal.
items.hint: Tenths live in the first spot after the point.
items.explanation: Six tenths = 6/10 = 0.6 — one place after the point, exactly where tenths belong.

items.prompt: Vet day! Biscuit weighs 4.09 kg and Mochi weighs 4.1 kg. Which cat is heavier?
items.hint: Pad to the same length: compare 4.10 with 4.09.
items.explanation: 4.10 > 4.09, so Mochi wins by a hundredth — longer decimals are NOT automatically bigger.

items.prompt: A potion in Charms club is 0.7 brewed. Tap 0.7 on the progress line.
items.hint: 0.7 is 7 tenths — count seven ticks past 0.
items.explanation: The line from 0 to 1 is cut into tenths, and 0.7 is the seventh tick.

items.prompt: Amal's lace knitting needle is 2.35 mm across. Tap 2.35 on the zoomed-in line.
items.hint: 2.35 sits exactly halfway between 2.3 and 2.4.
items.explanation: On a line marked in 0.05s, 2.35 is seven ticks past 2 — zooming in just reveals more tenths-of-tenths.

items.prompt: Which number is the LARGEST?
items.hint: Pad them all to thousandths, then compare like whole numbers.
items.explanation: Padded: 0.540 > 0.500 > 0.450 > 0.405 — comparing place by place settles it.

items.prompt: Compute: 4.8 ÷ 0.6
items.hint: Slide both decimal points one place right first.
items.explanation: 4.8 ÷ 0.6 = 48 ÷ 6 = 8 — making the divisor whole makes the problem friendly.

items.prompt: Write 3/8 as a decimal.
items.hint: A fraction bar is a division sign: compute 3 ÷ 8.
items.explanation: 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375 — every fraction converts by dividing top by bottom.

items.prompt: Sort each decimal: less than one half, or more than one half?
items.hint: Compare the tenths digit to 5 first — only ties need a deeper look.
items.explanation: 0.505 sneaks past 0.5 by five thousandths, while 0.099 never even reaches one tenth.

items.prompt: Order these decimals from smallest to largest.
items.hint: Give every number three decimal places first — then it's a fair race.
items.explanation: Padded to 0.093, 0.309, 0.390, 0.900, the order jumps right out — digits only count from their places.

items.prompt: Power-of-Ten Lightning! Slide those decimal points.
items.hint: Count the zeros — that's how many places the point hops.
items.explanation: ×10 hops the point right, ÷10 hops it left — one hop per zero, every time.

items.prompt: Switch costumes both ways.

lines: As a fraction in simplest form: 0.8 = [[4/5]]

items.hint: 9/20 stretches to hundredths; 0.8 starts as 8/10 and then simplifies.
items.explanation: 9/20 = 45/100 = 0.45, and 0.8 = 8/10 = 4/5 — decimals and fractions are the same numbers in different outfits.

items.prompt: Café receipt: Amal buys a $3.65 croissant and a $1.85 hot cocoa, paying with a $10 bill. Finish the receipt.
items.hint: Add the treats first; the change is what's left of the 10.
items.explanation: 3.65 + 1.85 = 5.50 and 10.00 − 5.50 = 4.50 — lined-up points kept every cent accounted for.

items.prompt: A goblin accountant multiplied 0.5 × 0.3. Tap the step where the work went wrong.

segments: Step B: count decimal places — one in each factor, two in all

items.hint: Step B counted TWO places. Did Step C use both?
items.explanation: Two decimal places turn 15 into 0.15, not 1.5. Estimate check: half of 0.3 can't possibly be 1.5!

items.prompt: Legendary: a spool holds 6 m of cord. Amal cuts as many 0.35 m friendship-bracelet cords as possible. How many METERS of cord are left over?
items.hint: Slide both points: 6 ÷ 0.35 → 600 ÷ 35. The whole-number part says how many cords; then find what they used.
items.explanation: 600 ÷ 35 = 17 remainder 5, so 17 cords use 17 × 0.35 = 5.95 m, leaving 0.05 m. Tracking the remainder back to meters is the legendary move.

items.prompt: Legendary: butterbeer-style cream soda costs $2.35 a bottle. Amal buys 4 bottles for movie night and pays with a $10 bill. How much change does she get, in dollars?
items.hint: Total first (2.35 × 4), then subtract from 10.00.
items.explanation: 2.35 × 4 = $9.40 and 10.00 − 9.40 = $0.60. Lining up those decimal points kept every cent honest.
